html:
The Ok Tedi copper and gold mine in western Papua New Guinea has dumped large amounts of waste into the Ok Tedi and Fly rivers since the 1980s, after its tailings dam collapsed during building.

The waste raised riverbeds, flooded forests and gardens, and killed fish along hundreds of kilometres. Villagers downstream sued BHP, the main owner, in an Australian court and won a settlement in 1996.

BHP left the mine in 2002, handing its share to a fund for the country. The mine remains a large part of the national economy. With the Panguna conflict, it shaped debates on mining across the Pacific. See also Papua New Guinea and Fly River.
sum: The Ok Tedi copper and gold mine in western Papua New Guinea has dumped large amounts of waste into the Ok Tedi and Fly rivers since the 1980s, after its tailings dam collapsed during building.
